transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-06
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: Yes
Attendees: Alex Murphy (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Redwood SA); Daniel Park (QDR Head of Infrastructure), Maya Singh (QDR Compliance), Roberto Cruz (QDR Embedded Lead), Lina Holt (Procurement), Tom Weaver (Ops)

Summary:
QDR is evaluating a fully air-gapped on-prem deployment for highly regulated telemetry processing. Primary concerns: signed firmware/update workflow, HSM/KMS integration for keys, offline telemetry retention, hardware spec (H100 vs A100), maintenance/patch windows, and vendor access controls. They want a pilot (single rack) and a clear documented flow for offline updates via courier/USB with attestations.

Topics:
- Credentialed update process and firmware signing
- Hardware compatibility and benchmarking expectations
- Ops runbook for firmware/patching in sealed facilities
- Compliance artifacts (SOC/ISO/FIPS/attestations)
- Pricing and pilot scope

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Daniel: Daniel Park here.
[00:06] Maya: Maya Singh, compliance.
[00:07] Roberto: Roberto Cruz.
[00:08] Lina: Lina Holt.
[00:10] Tom: Tom Weaver, ops.
[00:12] Alex: Great, from Redwood we've got Priya and Jared as well. The goal for today is to walk through your air-gap requirements and clarify assumptions so we can scope a pilot and the security artifacts you'll need.
[00:24] Priya: Real quick, if I could add — we'd like to capture the exact firmware/signing constraints. QDR previously mentioned FIPS HSM and that images must be signed by your side, correct?
[00:34] Maya: Yes, everything that goes into the sealed racks must be signed by our approved PKI and we require a verifiable chain of custody. No inbound SSH or push from any external network.
[00:45] Priya: OK, good. Redwood's private package supports signed images and we can either integrate with an on-prem HSM or work with our signing pipeline to produce signed bundles that you verify locally. We'll need to confirm which model you prefer.
[00:58] Daniel: Prefer on-prem HSM. We have a Thales Luna already in our compliant room. Can Redwood plug into a customer-provided HSM, or do you require Redwood-managed keys?
[01:10] Jared: We support customer-managed HSMs via standard PKCS#11 interfaces for key wrapping and signing. There are a couple of modes: 1) Redwood produces the image and signs with a Redwood-managed key, then you re-sign with your HSM at intake; or 2) Redwood provides unsigned artifacts and you sign entirely in-house. For most customers in your situation we propose Redwood provides verified image artifacts plus a signing manifest that you apply with your HSM before deployment.
[01:36] Maya: That manifest needs to include the build hash, image manifest, and a signed SBOM. Also we need attestations for the build pipeline.
[01:44] Priya: We can generate SBOMs and build provenance from our compilation step. One note, some model compilation optimizations are hardware-specific — if you plan to run on H100 with certain kernel choices the binary layout changes and we'd need to produce a matching manifest.
[01:58] Roberto: So that means if we change from A100 to H100 the image you give us could be different and we'd have to re-sign?
[02:05] Priya: Correct. We typically produce a family of artifacts per hardware profile. We can minimize churn by using a compatibility layer but for top performance we recommend hardware-specific builds.
[02:16] Tom: For operations, our constraint is we only get weekly maintenance windows and the sealed facility only allows courier-delivered USB media with tamper-evident seals. Can you describe the update flow you envision?
[02:29] Jared: Sure. Draft flow: Redwood generates artifacts -> artifacts sent to QDR via SFTP out-of-band or secure courier (for sealed sites we do courier) -> QDR imports into local signing HSM -> operator runs integrity checks using SHA/manifest -> HSM signs the image -> operator installs via offline load utility -> post-installation attestation report is generated and returned to Redwood if requested.
[02:54] Daniel: Do you offer the local install utility? We try to avoid bespoke tooling; prefer something vendor-neutral.
[03:02] Priya: We provide a cross-platform offline installer (CLI) that runs in a restricted shell. It doesn't phone-home. It's basically a deterministic unpack and verify then write to the node. We also provide a NIST-style verification script.
[03:14] Maya: The verification script must output signed attestation that includes operator identity and HSM signature.
[03:20] Priya: Yes, we can include an attestation helper that calls into the PKCS#11 module and produces a signed attestation blob.
[03:27] Lina: Procurement question — what's the minimum pilot configuration and lead time for hardware? We're considering one rack to start.
[03:34] Alex: Typical pilot is one rack with 4x H100 SXM (or 4x A100 if you prefer), 1 head node, and 1 management appliance. Lead time depends on availability but for H100s realistically 6-8 weeks for full procurement; on a dedicated pilot we can also run hosted validation in our environment first — that shortens the iterations.
[03:55] Roberto: We have spare A100s but if we need the H100 perf profiles for your kernel it'll matter. What throughput can we expect? We process large telemetry bursts — short sequences but high concurrency.
[04:08] Priya: If sequences are short (<=128 tokens) and you optimize batching, a 4x H100 rack with our runtime should handle roughly 800-1,200 concurrent qps-ish for single-token-ish responses — that's a very rough back-of-envelope, we'd want to run a benchmark with your prompt distribution.
[04:26] Daniel: OK please note we need latency SLOs < 150ms p95 for inference.
[04:30] Priya: Understood, we'll validate with the exact prompt set in the pilot. P95s depend heavily on batch windows and KV cache hit rates.
[04:39] Maya: Back to compliance — we need audit logs for all update actions, and the logs must be write-once and exported to our SIEM. Can Redwood produce logs that are signable and exportable?
[04:50] Jared: Yes, the private package writes tamper-evident audit trails (append-only) and we can ship logs as syslog or a signed bundle. We can also integrate with your SIEM via a scheduled physical export.
[05:01] Alex: Quick note on access — customers typically want RBAC and SSO for consoles. In your air-gapped setup, would you want local SAML/SSO or a jump-hosted SSO?
[05:12] Daniel: Local SAML is preferred. We run an internal IdP in the sealed zone.
[05:16] Priya: Our private control plane supports local SAML and can be configured to talk to an internal IdP. We can also run in a mode where there is no persistent control plane outside the site — admin actions are batched and applied during maintenance.
[05:28] Tom: About support — how do technicians debug issues if Redwood can't access the environment? We'll need CLEAR support runbooks and optionally an on-site consultant.
[05:36] Alex: For fully air-gapped customers we provide detailed runbooks and can schedule remote screen-share sessions where the customer runs diagnostics. For critical incidents we offer an on-prem consultant under an add-on contract. We also have a hot-swap image that operators can load to collect traces.
[05:51] Maya: The runbook must include escalation matrix and a list of exact artifacts Redwood will request — hashed bundles only, never raw logs with PII.
[05:58] Priya: We'll prepare a compliance pack that lists all required artifacts and a redacted logging option. We'll also include a template NDA for on-site support visits.
[06:08] Roberto: Two technical details: 1) our racks are air-conditioned but we have an older switch fabric; 2) firmware signing needs to cover UEFI boot and signed kernel modules. Can you sign bootloaders?
[06:18] Jared: We can provide signed bootloader images and kernel modules as part of the manifest. If you want UEFI Secure Boot we recommend an MOK-style (Machine Owner Key) flow where your HSM signs the key and you enroll it locally.
[06:29] Roberto: Enrollment is manual; we have a process. Any chance of automatic key rotation when there's no network?
[06:35] Priya: Key rotation in fully isolated zones is manual. We can automate the tooling that generates rotation bundles which you then approve and sign in the HSM. That bundle can be applied during the maintenance window.
[06:46] Daniel: What about attestations for model provenance? We need to show regulators the model weights haven't been tampered with.
[06:53] Priya: We produce a signed model checksum and an SBOM that includes parameter fingerprints. We can also run a deterministic model validation step (byte-level hash) that you can verify post-deployment.
[07:03] Maya: Any certifications Redwood has that are relevant? SOC 2 Type II we know, but do you have FIPS 140-2/3 compliance or ISO27001 for the private stack?
[07:12] Alex: Redwood's hosted platform is SOC 2 Type II. Our private package vendors and partners maintain ISO27001 and we can provide documentation on FIPS-validated modules for cryptography. We don't claim FIPS certification for the runtime itself but we integrate with FIPS-validated HSMs. We'll attach the compliance bundle.
[07:28] Lina: Procurement question: what are the terms for software updates and who owns Sealed Image signing keys?
[07:35] Alex: Short answer: keys are customer-owned in your preferred mode. Software updates covered under a subscription; large security patches can be delivered via the signed-image flow. Pricing depends on deployment mode (private perpetual license + annual support) — we'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[07:48] Tom: How do you handle emergency patches that need to be applied outside the weekly window? We sometimes have CVEs that are critical.
[07:55] Jared: We have an emergency patch path: Redwood produces an emergency signed bundle and we coordinate a courier or encrypted air-gapped transfer. For truly urgent CVEs, we can also dispatch an on-site engineer under an expedited support contract.
[08:08] Daniel: Customer-side gating: who needs to sign off internally for pilot acceptance?
[08:12] Daniel: For us it's infrastructure, compliance, and procurement.
[08:16] Maya: Compliance will sign off on security artifacts and runbook.
[08:18] Lina: Procurement on contract terms and commercials.
[08:20] Priya: Great — that gives us a checklist for pilot acceptance criteria: successful offline install, attestation signed by your HSM, end-to-end smoke test with your sample prompts, and performance within 20% of the validated hosted baseline.
[08:34] Daniel: On sample prompts — we'll share a redacted prompt set and load profile. Do you need full logs during the pilot?
[08:40] Priya: We'll request anonymized telemetry for performance debugging, but only if you authorize and after we redaction step.
[08:48] Tom: Another ops detail — we run non-root installers in locked consoles. Will your installer require escalated privileges?
[08:54] Priya: The installer needs local write to specific device nodes but we can run it as a signed setuid helper or through a designated service account. We'll adapt to your constraints.
[09:04] Maya: We also require that any third-party libs in the runtime be listed. SBOM request again.
[09:09] Priya: We'll provide SBOMs for all runtime artifacts.
[09:12] Alex: Quick check — are there any vendor access restrictions beyond the courier and signed images? For example, no remote SSH, no inbound VPN, zero external telemetry?
[09:23] Daniel: Correct. Zero inbound connections, telemetry exported only via scheduled physical export. No remote exec except under tightly controlled on-site sessions.
[09:33] Roberto: We use an internal KVM for consoles; if you need to triage we'll be sharing KVM sessions.
[09:38] Jared: That's workable. We'll document the session protocol and the artifacts we need in advance.
[09:44] Alex: Let's talk about timeline for pilot and milestones. We propose: kick off week of July 12, hardware inventory and procurement by July 12-23, image build and compatibility validation by July 26, pilot install week Aug 9 (in your maintenance window). Does that align?
[09:59] Daniel: Procurement lead time for H100s may push us into late August. If we start with A100s we could do August earlier.
[10:07] Priya: We can run hosted baseline tests on Redwood's infra in July using your prompt set while hardware lead times get sorted. That will help verify perf expectations before on-prem install.
[10:16] Maya: We'll need to see the compliance pack before sign-off to commit to dates.
[10:20] Alex: We'll send the security/compliance pack and a pilot SOW by Friday 2027-07-08.
[10:27] Lina: On commercials, do you have a standard pilot pricing or a credit?
[10:31] Alex: Typically pilots are discounted; we include X weeks of support and a cost estimate for the private license and optional on-site support. We'll include an estimate in the SOW.
[10:39] Tom: Any gotchas you see from similar customers?
[10:42] Priya: Two common ones: 1) underestimate of key rotation complexity in isolated sites, and 2) underestimating the number of signed artifacts when you have multiple microcode/firmware layers. Both increase operations overhead. We recommend planning a maintenance cadence and signing SOP upfront.
[10:58] Roberto: For the microcode thing — do you have guidance on vendor BIOS/firmware signing? Some of our older nodes don't support vendor-signed UEFI.
[11:06] Jared: We can provide guidance but for older hardware you might need a firmware update path from the OEM. We can assist with a validated image but we can't substitute OEM-signed firmware for BIOS unless you enroll a machine-owner key.
[11:18] Maya: Are there any legal artifacts we should expect? For example, a data-handling addendum or shared responsibility matrix?
[11:24] Alex: Yes, we'll include a private deployment addendum that clarifies responsibility for keys, data residency, maintenance windows, and access. We'll also include an NDA template for on-site visits.
[11:34] Daniel: One more question — telemetry retention. We need to retain telemetry locally for 7 years per regs and redact PII automatically. Can Redwood's runtime enforce retention policies?
[11:44] Priya: The runtime supports configurable retention and automatic redaction filters. For long-term storage we recommend exporting to your local WORM storage or tape via scheduled export.
[11:54] Maya: We'll want to see the redaction rules and confirm they meet our legal team's thresholds.
[11:59] Priya: We'll include the redaction policy doc and example artifacts.
[12:04] Alex: Sounds like we have what we need to scope the pilot. Recap of deliverables: Redwood sends security/compliance pack, signing spec, pilot SOW + pricing; QDR sends hardware inventory and maintenance window; schedule technical deep-dive week of July 19.
[12:22] Daniel: Agreed.
[12:23] Lina: Agreed.
[12:24] Maya: Agreed.
[12:25] Alex: Any final questions?
[12:28] Tom: Not from ops.
[12:29] Roberto: One final ask — can you include a short checklist we can run in a test lab to pre-validate the installer?
[12:35] Priya: Yes, we'll include a lab checklist and a small automated harness you can run in your staging environment.
[12:41] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by Friday.
[12:46] Daniel: Thanks all.
[12:47] Meeting ends.
